_comment: Procedural table for NPCs. Per procedural_generation_scope_proposal.md #2, NPCs are the deepest 'partial fit' -- traits/speech/roleArchetype/age come from these tables, but physicalDescription/contradiction/wants/actuallyNeeds/questHook/dialogue are genuinely freeform, so lib/proceduralGenerators.js fills them from Mad-Libs templates below rather than leaving them blank. faction is picked from the world's own live faction roster (or 'unaligned'); roleArchetype values match render.js's CATEGORY_SORT npc order list exactly so procedurally-generated NPCs group/sort correctly on the index page. Every genre-filtered row below carries a `genre` array (post_apoc/fantasy/scifi/modern/horror, or `universal` for anything genre-agnostic) -- see lib/proceduralGenerators.js's 'Genre awareness' section for how detectGenreBuckets()/filterByGenre() use it. roleArchetypes/ages/dialogueBranches/designNotes are NOT genre-filtered by the code and intentionally carry no genre field.

physicalDescriptionTemplates.value: {pronoun_cap} {carries} {pronoun_pos} weight like someone used to being underestimated for it -- deliberate, unhurried, never quite still.
A face that's clearly been through something, worn in exactly the places that show it. {pronoun_cap} {dresses} like comfort matters more than appearance, and it shows.
Sharp-eyed and a little too observant for casual conversation. {pronoun_cap} {has} the look of someone who's already sized up the room before you noticed them in it.
Compact, practical, dressed for whatever the day turns into. Hands that have clearly done real work, whatever {pronoun_pos} current job title says.
Taller than the room usually expects, and {pronoun_subj} {seems} aware of it -- angles {pronoun_pos} posture to take up less space than {pronoun_pos} actually does.

{pronoun_cap} {carries} {pronoun_pos} blade the way some people carry a walking stick -- more habit than threat, though no less ready for it. Travel-worn cloak, boots that have crossed three kingdoms at least.

A face suited to a tapestry rather than a tavern -- striking in a way that clearly troubles {pronoun_pos} composure. {pronoun_cap} {dresses} plainly, as if trying to be overlooked, and mostly failing.
Weathered in the way of someone who's slept under more roofs made of sky than timber. {pronoun_cap} {has} the calluses of a trade never named outright.
An old scar sits along {pronoun_pos} jaw like a story {pronoun_subj} {seems} almost proud of, and a bearing that suggests a life once spent in a hall that no longer stands.

{pronoun_cap} {dresses} in layers of mismatched finery and practical leather, like two different lives got folded into one wardrobe. {pronoun_cap} {carries} {pronoun_pos} coin purse suspiciously close at hand.
{pronoun_cap} {carries} {pronoun_pos} augments the way most people carry a bad habit -- visible if you know where to look. {pronoun_cap} {seems} tired of explaining them to people who ask.

Sleek, efficient, faintly synthetic under the light. {pronoun_cap} {seems} built for a station corridor more than open ground, and {pronoun_cap} {dresses} in tech-weave that's seen better maintenance cycles.
A face reconstructed at least once, well enough that only a trained eye catches the seams. {pronoun_cap} {has} the stillness of someone used to zero-g.
{pronoun_cap} {carries} {pronoun_pos} gear like it's an extension of {pronoun_pos} own arm, which, depending who's asking, it might actually be.
Pale under artificial light, the kind that suggests real sun is a distant memory. {pronoun_cap} {dresses} for function over anything else.
{pronoun_cap} {dresses} like someone who got ready in a hurry and made it work anyway. {pronoun_cap} {carries} {pronoun_pos} phone like it might ring with bad news any second.
Ordinary in exactly the way that makes {pronoun_pos} job easier -- the kind of face that's hard to describe five minutes after {pronoun_subj} {has} left the room.
{pronoun_cap} {has} the posture of someone who spends too long at a desk and knows it. {pronoun_cap} {seems} perpetually one meeting behind.
Comfortable clothes, tired eyes, a coffee gone cold that {pronoun_subj} {seems} to have forgotten about entirely.
{pronoun_cap} {dresses} a little sharper than the job requires, like {pronoun_subj} {seems} always halfway to convincing someone of something.
{pronoun_cap} {seems} almost too still between sentences, in a way that takes a moment too long to place as wrong.
There's something slightly off about the way {pronoun_subj} {seems} to track movement in the room -- a beat too slow, or a beat too fast, never quite in rhythm with the conversation.
{pronoun_cap} {dresses} like the weather stopped mattering years ago, and {pronoun_pos} smile arrives a half-second after it should.
Pale in a way that reads more like habit than health. {pronoun_cap} {has} the look of someone who sleeps with the light on, for reasons {pronoun_subj} {seems} unwilling to name.
{pronoun_cap} {carries} {pronoun_pos} belongings like {pronoun_subj} {seems} ready to leave very suddenly, and {pronoun_subj} {seems} already listening for the reason why.

contradictionTemplates.value: Preaches self-sufficiency to everyone who'll listen, and quietly does favors nobody asked for.
Claims to have no patience for sentiment, keeps every letter anyone's ever written them.
Talks like they've made peace with how things turned out. They haven't.
Insists they don't play favorites, and everyone here knows exactly who the favorite is.
Says trust is earned, not given -- then extends it faster than anyone realizes until it's too late to take back.
Acts like the past is settled business. It comes up in almost every conversation anyway.

wantsTemplates.value: To be the reason this place is still standing, whether or not anyone ever knows it.
One clean win that isn't a compromise, for once.
To settle a score that's been open long enough to feel like part of the furniture.
For someone specific to finally admit they were right.
Enough stability to stop planning for the worst constantly.
To matter to people who don't need anything from them.
To be knighted before their family name is forgotten entirely.
To see the old kingdom's borders restored in their lifetime, however unlikely that's become.
To be remembered in a song, even an unflattering one.
To buy back a contract that never should have been signed away in the first place.
To see planetside sky again before running out of reasons to try.
To finally make partner, or quit trying to pretend that's still the plan.
To pay off the house before anyone finds out how close it came to being lost.
For whatever's in the walls to finally just show itself, so at least the waiting would stop.
To be believed, just once, by someone who matters.

actuallyNeedsTemplates.value: To let go of a decision that can't be undone.
To be told, and believe, that they're not actually responsible for everything that's gone wrong.
Someone to actually rely on, instead of everyone relying on them.
To forgive a version of themselves that no longer exists.
To stop treating every relationship as a transaction.
Rest they will not admit to needing.

speechRegisters.value: Blunt and economical -- says exactly as much as needed, no more.
Formal, almost old-fashioned, even in casual conversation.
Warm and conversational, quick to bring strangers in.
Clipped and professional, like everything's a negotiation.
Rambling and tangent-prone, circles back eventually.

speechRhythms.value: Short sentences. Rarely elaborates unless pushed.
Long, winding sentences that eventually land somewhere.
Speaks in lists -- first this, then that, then the other thing.
Pauses before anything important, like weighing the cost of saying it.
Talks fast when nervous, slows down deliberately when it matters.

speechTics.value: Ends questions with a small, humorless laugh.
Repeats the last few words of what you just said back at you.
Says "look" before anything they actually mean.
Taps twice on whatever surface is nearest when thinking.
Calls everyone "friend," including people they clearly don't trust.
Trails off mid-sentence and expects you to fill in the rest.

neverSayLines.value: "The crown was right to banish me."

signatureQuotes.value: You get one version of me. This is it.
Everyone wants something. At least I'm honest about it.
I've buried better plans than whatever you've got.
Ask nicely and I might even tell you the truth.
Around here, favors are the only real currency.
I stopped being surprised by people a long time ago.
The gods left this world a long time ago. The rest of us just haven't noticed yet.
A blade only lies if the hand behind it does.
I've buried three kings and outlived every one of their promises.
Magic doesn't forgive carelessness. Neither do I.
Every oath has a price. Mine's already been paid.
The realm remembers, even when its people don't.
Out here, the only law that holds is the one you enforce yourself.
Every system fails eventually. The trick is not being the one holding it when it does.
The Company owns the ship. It doesn't own me.
Signal's down again. So's my patience.
I've seen what's past the edge of the map. It's not worth the trip.
Augments don't make you better. They just make your mistakes faster.
Everyone's got an angle. I just stopped pretending I don't.
You want the truth or the version that doesn't get me sued?
This city eats people who slow down.
I've got a mortgage and no illusions left. Ask your question.
Nobody reads the fine print until it's too late.
I've survived worse meetings than this one.
You don't want to know what's actually down there. Trust me on that one thing.
I stopped asking why a long time ago. Asking why gets you noticed.
It doesn't come if you don't say its name. So we don't say its name.
Some doors get left shut for a reason. That one's staying shut.
I don't sleep well. I sleep at all. That's the win these days.
Whatever you heard, it was worse in person.

dialogueOpeningLines.value: Didn't expect company today. What do you need?
You've got about a minute before I get back to actual work.
I know that look. Someone sent you, or you're lost.
If you're here to complain, get in line.
Careful. I bite when I'm interrupted.
State your business, traveler, before the guards do it for you.
You've the look of someone who needs something. Everyone does, eventually.
Mind the wards at the door. They don't much care for strangers.
Another one seeking the old ruins, I'd wager. They rarely come back different.
Sit, if you like. The road makes liars of everyone eventually, so speak plainly.
The gods sent you, or you're lost. Either way, you're here now.
Signal's clean. State your business before someone flags this channel.
You're either lost or looking for trouble. This station only has the second kind.
Docking fees are non-negotiable. Everything else, we can talk about.
Careful with the airlock behind you. It doesn't like being ignored.
You've got clearance to be here, or you've got a very good story. Which is it?
Another drifter looking for work. Fine. Let's see if you're worth the fuel.
If you're selling something, I've already got too much of it.
You've got that look. Everyone who comes in here does, eventually.
Traffic was bad, or you're stalling. Either way, talk fast.
I've got maybe five minutes before my phone starts blowing up again.
Whatever this is, tell me it's not another problem.
You found me. Congratulations. What do you need?
You shouldn't be out this late. Neither should I, honestly.
Lock the door behind you. Habit, not paranoia. Probably.
Say what you need quickly. I don't like leaving the lights off for long.
You heard something too, didn't you. That's why you're here.
Don't mind the noise upstairs. It's usually nothing.
I wasn't expecting anyone. Especially not tonight.

dialogueBranches.reply: Alright, alright -- come in, sit down. I'll even pretend I wasn't busy.
That depends entirely on who's asking, and why.
Fine. Let's not waste each other's time, then.

designNotes.value: Rolled procedurally -- structured fields (traits, speech, role) are solid, but physicalDescription/contradiction/wants/questHook/dialogue are Mad-Libs placeholders worth a manual or field-assist pass before this NPC carries real weight in a scene.
